skill.name: party-drink-planner

skill.summary: Turn approved event assumptions into reconciled beverage, package, inventory, and cocktail ingredient quantities.

content.value_statement: Event hosts need accurate beverage quantities without hidden consumption assumptions. This skill converts approved inputs into reviewable servings, packages, inventory gaps, and ingredient totals.
actual_capabilities: Validates guest counts, duration, jurisdiction, beverage mix, planning assumptions, package yields, and optional inventory.
Allocates approved alcoholic servings across beer, wine, and cocktails using the largest-remainder method.
Rounds beer units, wine bottles, and spirit bottles upward from user-supplied package yields.
Subtracts known inventory from required packages and reports remaining gaps.
Scales named cocktail recipes into fluid ounces and milliliters while preserving unknown inventory states.
Calculates nonalcoholic servings, water liters, and ice quantities from supplied assumptions.
limitations: The skill does not select universal serving rates or provide personal drinking guidance.
Calculation requires Python 3 and a local JSON input file that follows the documented contract.
The skill does not verify local package labels, alcohol laws, or service rules.
The skill does not purchase supplies, track live service, schedule preparation, or manage recurring inventory.

use_cases.title: Estimate a private party
use_cases.description: Convert a host-approved guest plan into beverage servings, package counts, water, ice, and alcohol-free quantities.

use_cases.title: Reconcile event inventory
use_cases.description: Compare required beer, wine, spirits, and recipe ingredients against known stock before human review.

use_cases.title: Scale a cocktail menu
use_cases.description: Allocate cocktail servings across named recipes and calculate ingredient totals from supplied per-serving measures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic beverage plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan beverages for [total] guests, including [drinking] drinking guests, over [hours] hours in [country]. Use the approved assumptions and source I provide. Report any missing required fields before calculation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a reviewed event plan without inventing assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Include available inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Calculate my approved event scenario using mix [shares], package yields [yields], and buffer [percent]. Subtract this inventory: [counts]. Present servings, packages, remaining gaps, water, ice, and alcohol-free quantities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Determine remaining supply gaps from stock already available.

prompt_templates.title: Scale named cocktails
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved scenario and assign [share] of cocktail servings to each named recipe. Scale every supplied ingredient measure. Show ounces, milliliters, known inventory, and unresolved gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare reviewable ingredient quantities for a cocktail menu.

prompt_templates.title: Compare approved scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Calculate these separately approved scenarios one at a time: [scenario A] and [scenario B]. Reconcile each result. Then compare servings, package counts, inventory gaps, water, ice, and assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare independently approved event plans without creating default rates.

output_examples.input: Plan for 24 guests, 18 drinking guests, four approved servings each, a 10 percent buffer, supplied yields, inventory, and one Daiquiri recipe.
output: Allocation: 28 beer servings, 20 wine servings, and 32 cocktail servings.
Packages: 28 beer units, 4 wine bottles, and 2 spirit bottles.
Inventory gaps: 16 beer units, 2 wine bottles, and 1 spirit bottle.
Alcohol-free plan: 72 servings, 28.8 liters of water, and 36 pounds of ice.

output_examples.input: Plan an approved 12-guest event with no drinking guests, three alcohol-free servings per guest, water, and ice assumptions.
output: Alcoholic plan: zero servings, zero packages, and zero inventory gaps.
Alcohol-free plan: 36 servings, 14.4 liters of water, and 8.2 kilograms of ice.
Review state: the supplied assumptions and jurisdiction remain visible.

best_practices: Provide every planning assumption with its source, approver, and review date.
Use package yields from the actual products or a clearly declared planning convention.
Review beverage allocations, package coverage, recipe totals, units, and unknown inventory before acting.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent a universal servings rate from guest count or duration.
Do not omit beverage shares, package yields, source details, or other required assumptions.
Do not treat absent inventory as zero or present the supply estimate as personal drinking guidance.

faq.question: Does the skill decide how much each guest should drink?
faq.answer: No. A user or approved source must provide the planned servings assumption.

faq.question: What happens when required information is missing?
faq.answer: The skill stops and reports the missing fields instead of inventing values.

faq.question: Can it account for supplies already available?
faq.answer: Yes. It subtracts supplied package inventory and preserves unknown ingredient inventory as unknown.

faq.question: Can it calculate named cocktail ingredients?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide each recipe, its requested share, and positive per-serving ingredient measures.

faq.question: Does it check local alcohol rules?
faq.answer: No. Users remain responsible for local package labels, service rules, and legal requirements.

faq.question: Will it purchase supplies or manage ongoing inventory?
faq.answer: No. It produces a reviewable supply estimate and performs no purchase or recurring tracking action.
